THE KEY ENGINEERING CALL: M2-T1 cools LINEARLY against the iteration budget (temperature = half·(1−iter/iterations)); measured, that FREEZES rather than equilibrates — the raw residual energy sits at ~10–40 for most of a 2000-iteration run and only collapses in the final few steps (the cap holds the nodes far from balance until it vanishes) — and because the schedule depends on the budget, the same run at a different iteration count is a DIFFERENT shape. So it is a poor settlement rule. The settlement pass instead cools EXPONENTIALLY and INDEPENDENTLY of the budget (temperature(i) = half·decay^i, DEFAULT_DECAY = 0.98). Two things follow: (1) STABLE CONVERGENCE — the residual energy decays geometrically to floating-point zero (a real force balance), so the four fixtures converge in 770–834 iterations at residual <= 1e-6 (DEFAULT_ENERGY_TOLERANCE), well before DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS 2000; (2) REPRODUCIBLE RE-LAYOUT — because the trajectory depends only on the iteration INDEX, the settled configuration is BUDGET-INDEPENDENT: maxIterations 1500, 2000 and 8000 give byte-identical nodes (pinned by a test), which is the strongest available statement of 'stable re-layout'. Honesty: a two-agent graph with no links is reported converged:false with a non-zero final energy (repulsion-only has no finite equilibrium) rather than faked — reported, never invented. TO AVOID A SECOND FORCE LAW, layoutTrace's physics was extracted into a shared core in forceLayout.ts — prepareSimulation (build the seeded initial state), relaxIteration (one step; returns residual energy + the applied max node movement), buildLayout (freeze the state into a ForceLayout) — and layoutTrace was rewritten to drive it. Both primitives now share ONE physics and cannot drift; a source-level guard asserts settlement.ts imports the core. The extraction is byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving: all 28 M2-T1 tests still pass unchanged. The Settlement it returns carries converged, iterations, maxIterations, decay, energyTolerance, energyHistory, movementHistory, finalEnergy and finalMovement; isSettled(layout, tolerance?) reads a layout's residual force. The three named properties are gated as DATA over the fixtures (no visuals — jsdom has no GPU; the look is human-held M5-T5): STABLE CONVERGENCE (converged true, iterations < cap, finalEnergy <= tolerance, energy descends, a looser tolerance stops no later than a tighter one, degenerate 0/1-agent runs settle immediately); NO JITTER (every step is capped by that step's geometrically-decaying temperature, the last-100 movement history is monotone so the shape cannot oscillate, finalMovement < 1e-5, and a much larger budget settles to the identical shape); REPRODUCIBLE RE-LAYOUT (byte-identical across calls, independent of array order, budget-independent nodes, seed default/override). It also re-pins M2-T1's structural property (settlement does not break 'connected agents settle nearer than unconnected'). Pure and deterministic: no clock, no randomness, no model mutation. Deliberately NOT done here: the visual-attribute mapping (M2-T3), the typed spawn/handoff/message edge model (M2-T4), any render/three.js, and NO change to layoutTrace's fixed-budget defaults (M2-T1 stays as-is). NO SPREAD => NEUTRAL: when every agent has equal activity or every link equal volume there is no relative signal, so every element gets the midpoint (NEUTRAL_INTENSITY = 0.5) instead of 0/0. M2-T4.title: Derived edge model: spawn/handoff/message edges from the trace, never hand-placed
M2-T4.tests_added: src/layout/edges.test.ts — 36 tests. Shape: a fully-formed EdgeModel (expectTypeOf); EDGE_KINDS pinned to exactly ['spawn','handoff','message']; one lineage per agent in canonical id order; byKind groups equal the kind-filtered edges and counts agree; the edge list is ordered canonically (kind-rank, then source, then target). Classification: classifyAction reads a coordination verb (assign_task, start_loop, spawn_agent, delegate_work, dispatch, kickoff) as spawn, a relay verb (handoff / hand_off / hand-off / relay_task / escalate / transfer) as handoff, splits camelCase (assignTask -> spawn), checks handoff before spawn (relay_assign), and treats anything else — a draft, a revise, task_complete, assignment_complete, review_complete, '' or null — as an ordinary message (only the leading verb classifies). Per-fixture structure: fan-out is five orchestrator->worker spawn edges of weight 1 (actions ['assign_task']) with the orchestrator a coordinator and parent of all five (maxFanOut 5, rootIds [a_orchestrator]); loop is a kickoff spawn orchestrator->researcher beside two directed message edges (researcher<->critic, weight 3 each, actions draft / revise) and the never-spawned critic still reads worker; dead-branch is two orchestrator spawns plus a worker_ok->orchestrator task_complete message (maxFanOut 2); handoff-chain is the three-edge relay a->b->c->d with no spawn, every agent a root, the initiator a coordinator and the rest workers. Direction/targets: a two-way exchange stays TWO edges (not the collapsed layout link); a broadcast reaches every other agent and never its sender; a self-message contributes no edge; an inline action-bearing message classifies into spawn/handoff/message. Lineage: an agent that only ever receives is a participant (worker), not an invented 'external'; a spawn fan-in keeps both edges but picks the earliest spawner as parent; a spawn cycle throws DerivedEdgeError; an empty run is well-formed; an agent with no edges is 'unknown'. Lookups: lineageOf finds / returns null; edgeBetween is direction- and kind-specific. withDerivedLineage fills role/parentId, is a fixed point of normalizeTrace, accepts a pre-derived model, and does not mutate. Determinism: byte-identical across calls; independent of the array order; non-mutating. M2-T4.notes: M2-T4 adds the typed edge model to src/layout/edges.ts (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, no Math.random, no model mutation). deriveEdgeModel(model) turns the trace's messages into typed, DIRECTED relationships and, from the spawn edges, derives the two Agent fields M1-T5 deliberately deferred to this pass: role and parentId. THE THREE KINDS (the product's structural questions): spawn (a coordination act that puts another agent to work), handoff (the baton passing on), message (everything else). CLASSIFICATION IS DERIVED, NEVER HAND-PLACED: each message is classified from its declared action by matching the action's FIRST word (camelCase split, non-alphanumerics stripped) against verb tables — handoff checked before spawn; unmatched or action-less messages are plain 'message' edges, so the model never invents a stronger relationship than the trace states (assignment_complete is a message; assign_task is a spawn). DIRECTION IS PRESERVED: unlike deriveLayoutLinks (M2-T1, which collapses a pair into ONE undirected weighted link for the shape), this model keeps researcher->critic and critic->researcher as two edges — the relationship is directional (a spawn points at its child, a handoff at its successor). A broadcast yields one message edge to every other agent; a self-message contributes nothing. Edges aggregate by (kind, source, target) with weight/messageIds/actions/firstAt/lastAt and are sorted canonically (kind-rank, then source, then target). LINEAGE: parentId is the earliest spawner (deterministic tie-break by parent id when several agents spawn the same child — both spawn edges are kept, so fan-in stays visible); role is coordinator (spawns children, even if itself spawned — a sub-orchestrator), worker (was spawned, or otherwise participates), coordinator for the run's initiator, and unknown for an agent touched by nothing. ENGINEERING CALL: the first draft assigned an 'external' role to any agent that only ever received, but that mislabels a dead-branch terminal leaf and the end of a handoff chain as external — v1's agent_messages graph carries no signal that separates an external endpoint from a dead leaf, nor a human from an agent, so those two roles are NEVER invented here (documented; a plain sink reads worker). FAIL LOUDLY: a spawn cycle (an agent that is its own ancestor) throws DerivedEdgeError rather than being silently repaired — the same rule normalization uses. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): it iterates the model in canonical order and sorts its output, so the same trace yields a byte-identical EdgeModel whatever order the arrays arrive in (pinned by a test that reverses every array), and the model is never mutated. withDerivedLineage(model) writes the derived roles/parents back onto the contract and is a fixed point of normalizeTrace (M1-T5 preserves role/parentId), so a consumer can hand the render layer an enriched model. Deliberately NOT done here: re-deriving the layout adjacency (M2-T1 owns it), changing the visual mapping (M2-T3 shipped; wiring arcs to edge kinds is a later refinement), and the cross-fixture invariant sweep (M2-T5). NEXT: M2-T5 (layout + attribute invariant tests across all fixtures).

M3-T2.notes: M3-T2 lands the message-arc layer in the PRD §5 split: a PURE plan (src/scene/arcs.ts) + a PURE shader module (src/scene/arcShader.ts) + a THIN mesh (src/scene/MessageArcLayer.tsx). buildArcScenePlan(model, options?) sweeps ONE TUBE PER COMMUNICATION LINK into a SINGLE batched geometry: the curve is a quadratic Bezier from the source's settled position to the target's, bowed off the chord along perpendicularOf(chord) — the world axis the chord is least aligned with, crossed with it, so the bow axis is deterministic and never near-degenerate — and the tube ((segments+1) x sides vertices, triangle index buffer wound CCW about the outward radial) is swept with a PARALLEL-TRANSPORTED frame so it cannot twist. PRD GEOMETRY BUDGET HONOURED: the batch unit is the LINK, not the message — deriveLayoutLinks already collapsed every message between a pair into one weighted channel — so the whole population lands in one geometry drawn in ONE call (ARC_LAYER_DRAW_CALLS, reported as plan.drawCalls for M3-T5 to aggregate); no per-message mesh and no per-link mesh either; an empty layer costs 0 draw calls. THE ANIMATION IS DERIVED, NOT DECORATIVE: each arc carries a pulse RATE lerped from its normalized volume (M2-T3's own intensity) and a travel DIRECTION taken from the channel's NET traffic — forward and backward message counts, canonically oriented, computed with the same broadcast rule deriveLayoutLinks uses, so forward+backward === the link's weight exactly (pinned by tests). A BALANCED channel (equal traffic both ways) gets speed 0 and PARKED_PULSE_PHASE and simply does not travel: the trace shows no net direction there, and inventing one would be the same class of error as hand-placing a coordinate. (Flagged for the human look review — M5-T5 may prefer a different read of a balanced channel.) The per-pair phase is an FNV-1a hash of the pair, so arcs are not synchronised and nothing is random. The fixtures therefore read their own structure: the fan-out's five links all pulse outward, the loop's hot researcher<->critic channel is parked while its kickoff travels, the dead branch's unanswered assignment travels while the answered one parks, and the handoff relay travels a->b->c->d. THE SHADER IS GENERATED FROM THE PLAN'S CONTRACT: arcShader.ts builds its `attribute float ...;` lines from ARC_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES — the list the geometry writes — and its `uniform <type> <name>;` lines from ARC_UNIFORMS, the list buildArcUniforms fills, so a geometry attribute the shader forgot (or a shader attribute the geometry never provides) is structurally impossible; a test pins that two-way equality per stage, plus the varyings and the pulse formula. The GPU twin of the pure rule arcPulseParameter is `fract(uTime * aSpeed + aPhase)` flipped by `aFlow < 0.0`; the pure function is the reference implementation and a test asserts the GLSL keeps that shape — the same canary M3-T1 applies to three.js Matrix4.compose. THE CLOCK STAYS IN THE RENDER LAYER: uTime starts at 0 and MessageArcLayer advances it in useFrame (state.clock.elapsedTime); the pure layer takes time as a PARAMETER, so the rule is unit-testable in jsdom while the tick lives where the PRD puts it. Buffers are plain number[] (JSON-serialisable, deterministic) so the plan stays pure and three converts them to typed attributes on upload; the component builds ONE BufferGeometry, disposes it when the plan changes or it unmounts, and draws additively with depthWrite off, so nodes occlude arcs and arcs do not occlude each other. Viewport mounts the arc layer beside the node layer for the same run; both settle the layout independently and deterministically so they agree exactly, and M3-T6 is where the two derivations consolidate into one shared scene pass (which is also where the double settle should go before M5's scale work). NOT gated: the look (jsdom has no GPU; human-held M5-T5). The one artifact jsdom cannot exercise was instead verified out of band: the resolved shader text compiles under glslangValidator 16.6.0 for GLSL ES 1.00 and desktop GLSL 1.10 with a three.js-equivalent prefix, and the compiler rejects broken shaders, so the clean result means something. Deliberately NOT done here: the tool-call glyphs (M3-T3); the lighting/bloom emissive calibration (M3-T4) — the two colours and the glow constants are documented placeholders, not a calibration; colouring arcs by the M2-T4 edge KIND (that model refines relationships, not which channels exist); and the M3-T6 fixture mount. A glyph is one TOOL CALL — the adapter's derived unit of 'this agent did something' (M1-T4) — drawn as a mark orbiting the agent node that made the call, which is where the run's ACTIONS become visible spatially. buildGlyphScenePlan(model, options?) settles or reuses the layout (M2-T2), reuses or maps the attributes (M2-T3) and places one glyph per call: the ORBIT CENTRE is the caller's settled position (copied, never referenced, so a reused layout cannot mutate a built plan); the ORBIT RADIUS is the node's own mapped size + the glyph's own size/2 + a clearance (plus ring x ringGap for further concentric rings, DEFAULT_GLYPHS_PER_RING = 6 before stepping out) so a glyph's inner edge always clears the node surface; the ORBIT PLANE is a per-agent tilted frame whose normal is built from two hashed angles (tilt between 0.15 and 0.7 rad), with basis U from M3-T2's perpendicularOf and basis V = normal x U — hash-derived de-synchronisation, documented as such, the same role a hash plays for the arc pulse's phase, NOT a claim about the trace; the RATE is lerp(minOrbitHz, maxOrbitHz, the calling node's M2-T3 intensity), the same activity channel the arc pulse keys off, so 'busier' means faster everywhere; the KIND is M2-T4's classifyAction of the call's own action — this is why the task depends on M2-T4 — and it drives SIZE (kindScale 1.35/1.15/0.85) and HUE, the hue scaled by the caller's own emissive so a hot agent's glyphs read hotter. THE ANIMATION RULE IS PURE AND THE CLOCK IS THE RENDER LAYER'S: glyphOrbitAngle / glyphPositionAt / glyphMatrixAt take timeMs as a PARAMETER, and writeGlyphMatrices writes the whole batch straight into the InstancedMesh's own float32 buffer (offset and capacity honoured, only the output buffer mutated). The instance transform is composed with M3-T1's composeNodeMatrix rather than a second copy, so a glyph's matrix cannot drift from a node's convention (cross-checked against three.js Matrix4.compose). PRD GEOMETRY BUDGET HONOURED: the batch unit is the glyph — one InstancedMesh over a unit octahedron for the WHOLE population = exactly 1 draw call (GLYPH_LAYER_DRAW_CALLS, exported with plan.drawCalls so M3-T5's ceiling can aggregate it without re-deriving it); no per-glyph mesh anywhere; a run with no tool calls costs 0 draw calls (the layer returns null). An octahedron rather than a sphere on purpose: the mark must read as a mark on a node, not as a second smaller agent. Viewport mounts the layer beside the nodes and arcs when given a run; mounting a FIXTURE end-to-end stays M3-T6, which is also where the now-THREE independent layout settles should be consolidated into one shared scene pass (flagged as a look/perf item, not a correctness one). Design decisions worth keeping: the eye IS the fly state (first person has no sphere to derive it from) and it is always earned — seeded from a pose, then moved only by flyMove/flyAdvance; speed, wheel advance and the flight envelope are all multiples of the cloud's own radius so a 6-agent fixture and a 400-agent fleet feel the same; a frame's delta is capped at 100 ms (a backgrounded tab reports multi-second gaps) and a per-event wheel cap already existed; the composed movement direction is normalized rather than the axes, because world up is not perpendicular to a pitched look direction (normalizing the axes made "forward + rise" 11% SLOWER — caught by a test, fixed by normalizing the direction); the fly far plane is derived from the envelope (not the look distance) so turning round inside a big cloud never clips it; the drag convention is grab-the-world, identical to orbit, so a viewer who learned one does not relearn the other. One dedupe: the pose-apply code moved into applyPose.ts (both rigs use it — a second copy was a second chance to forget updateProjectionMatrix) and isTypingTarget moved into src/ui/keyboard.ts (the transport and the fly keys share one rule). LOOK OBSERVATIONS FOR M5-T5 (not asserted): in fly mode at the default opening pose the orchestrator node is a large saturated white disc — the same blow-out question M4-T2 raised, now seen from closer; and because the reveal is at the playhead, entering the scene at t=0 leaves most nodes dormant, so the first fly-in is mostly dark until the transport is scrubbed or played. Both are look calls for the human review, not defects this task should "fix". M4-T4.notes: M4-T4 keeps the PRD §5 split: TWO pure modules and a dumb panel. `inspect.ts` is the join that turns one agent's slice of the run into everything the panel shows — messages in both directions (a broadcast is received by every other agent, the same rule normalization and the layout use; the agent's own broadcast is SENT, not heard; a self-message appears once), tool calls, the activity window (first/last, offsets, share, quiet tail, tool time), the derived lineage and peers (from M2-T4's edge model, reused when the caller has one), and tokens/cost itemised per message sent and per tool call. ITEMISED ATTRIBUTION IS CHECKED AGAINST THE MODEL: `Agent.tokens`/`Agent.costUsd` are precomputed by M1-T5 from the same rules, so buildAgentDetail re-derives the parts and throws InspectError when the parts do not sum to the whole (tolerance 1e-9 relative, because summation order differs). A panel whose breakdown contradicts its own total is a defect, not a rounding note. ROLE/PARENT COME FROM THE DERIVED MODEL, not the contract fields the adapter leaves 'unknown'/null — so the panel agrees with the node colours and the spawn edges. `selection.ts` is the click vocabulary: instanceId→AgentId through the node plan's canonical instance order, and a gesture the pointer travelled across is NOT a click (R3F's ThreeEvent.delta, 4px slop) — without that an orbit released over the cloud would open a panel every time. Toggle is the reducer's rule (click the selected node to close, another to switch), a selection the run no longer has is cleared (useSelection), and the selected node is drawn at 1.6× its CALIBRATED radiance (a gain on the same curve the reveal uses, not a second calibration) — multiplied with the reveal, so a dormant selected node still dims. DELIBERATELY NOT RULES I INVENTED: no 'click the background to close' (the background is also the camera's drag surface, so an orbit would dismiss the panel the viewer just opened); Escape and the close button are the dismissals, and Escape is bound only while the panel is open (tests assert the listener is gone when closed). NO SECOND DERIVATION IN THE COMPONENT: the panel prints the pure model's strings/numbers (formatTokens/formatCost/formatShare, describeAgentTiming, describeMessageDirection) and slices lists to DETAIL_ROW_LIMIT=50 with a '+N more' note, so a 2k-message agent cannot put 2k rows in a 21rem panel. PLAYHEAD-AWARE WITHOUT OWNING TIME: every row carries `fired` computed from an elapsedMs passed in (no playhead → everything fired, matching the fully lit static scene), and pending rows are dimmed rather than hidden — structure persists, activity is revealed (M4-T1's philosophy). App owns the selection (useSelection) because the click, the scene highlight and the panel are three consumers of one fact. Deliberately NOT done: no Zustand store still (useReducer needs no dep), no filters/focus (M4-T5), no event list/search (anti-drift), no arc/glyph selection (highlighting a link would imply the link was selected — a different idea), no keyboard traversal of nodes. LOOK OBSERVATIONS FOR M5-T5 (not asserted, not a verdict): the orchestrator node renders as a large blown-out white disc at the default framing, and the 1.6× selected gain is INVISIBLE on it (an already-saturated node cannot get brighter) — selection currently reads from the panel's presence, not from the node, which is worth a human judgement call (a rim/halo or a dim-everything-else treatment would need geometry beyond this task); at t=0 most rows are dimmed pending, so the panel can read as 'mostly empty' until the transport moves; and the 21rem panel covers the right quarter of the `viewport`, hiding the rightmost worker nodes (gamma/epsilon) at the default framing — a collapse affordance may be the answer. M4-T5.notes: THE DESIGN CALL: the filter does NOT rebuild the scene. A second scene plan would re-settle the layout on every chip click and would make the gate measure a scene the app does not draw; instead filterRevealTrack narrows the EXISTING reveal track (the one M4-T1 already builds once per scene), so every filtered element falls out of the rules the reveal already pins — a node with no kept event has firstAt null and draws at DORMANT_NODE_GLOW, an arc with no kept message has volume 0 and draws at DORMANT_ARC_INTENSITY, a filtered-out glyph gets Infinity and never shows. Zero new brightness constants, zero duplicated arithmetic, and the identity filter is byte-identical to the unfiltered track (pinned for all four fixtures), which is the drift guard. STRUCTURE PERSISTS (the PRD rule): filtering never removes nodes, arcs or agents and never re-lays-out; it dims. FACET SEMANTICS (each a decision, all tested): the agent facet keeps messages an agent SENT or RECEIVED (so a worker lens keeps the assignment that created it) and credits a broadcast to any selected listener; an empty selection means every agent (the facet off) while an empty KIND selection means nothing matches — the honest reading, surfaced as a stated empty state in the bar rather than silently reverting to everything; the window is inclusive, in run-relative offsets, and NEVER rescales the transport (the scrubber still scrubs the whole run — a lens is not a different run). A node lights when it PARTICIPATES in a kept event, not only when it is selected, and that is exactly the rule the bar's 'N of M agents' count uses, so the number and the scene cannot disagree. FOCUS: toggling a chip off an unfiltered run keeps the other N-1, so a single-agent lens would cost N-1 clicks on a real fleet trace — hence double-click-to-isolate (onIsolateAgent/isolateAgentSelection, announced in the chip's tooltip rather than hidden). The filter and the inspector (M4-T4) stay independent on purpose: filtering does not close the panel and selecting does not filter the run. NOT HERE, DELIBERATELY: no text search and no transcript filter (PRD §8 — AgentReplay/traceview/tracediff own linear search), no per-link filtering, no saved/shareable filters (M6-T2 owns URL state), no filter-aware detail panel. LOOK OBSERVATION FOR M5-T5 (not a verdict, nothing asserted): a filtered-out element and a not-yet-fired element use the same dormant constants, so a viewer cannot tell 'outside the lens' from 'not reached yet' — the bar's summary line is the only cue. Whether that reads as clean or as ambiguous is a human judgement, and a distinct out-of-lens treatment (desaturate rather than dim, or a dimmed-but-tinted variant) would be the fix if it reads wrong. Also noted: with the fan-out fixture, deselecting the orchestrator keeps every message in view (they are all addressed to the selected workers), so a viewer may expect more narrowing than they get from a single chip click — the summary line is what makes that honest.
